Summary.Title: AURORA-17 Molecule-to-Market Flagship Demonstration Design
Summary.AssuranceEngineRule: Platform B and Platform B1 may evaluate assurance state and action admissibility. They do not independently execute regulated actions.
Summary.HumanAuthorityRule: Qualified humans and authorized organizational roles remain responsible for binding decisions.
Summary.SourceOfTruthRule: Official records and executed actions remain in governed source systems.
Summary.NoBindRule: Silence is a governance state. Silence is not consent. Insufficient binding conditions create an explicit governed hold.
Summary.Step156Statement: Step 156 is a design-only flagship demonstration baseline. It does not implement runtime workflows, manufacture a product, conduct a clinical trial, approve or release regulated work, use real patient data, or modify production systems.
Summary.Step157Gate: READY AFTER STEP 156 AURORA-17 FLAGSHIP DEMONSTRATION DESIGN REVIEW

DemonstrationObjects.CanonicalIdentityRule: One fictional program identity across all lifecycle stages.
Versioned candidate identity with AI-design provenance.
Protocol versions remain distinguishable and effective-date controlled.
Batch identity links materials, equipment, execution, QC, and release.
Product identifier, lot, serial, and transaction evidence remain linked.
Shipment, container, condition, and custody events use one governed identity.
Mock patient, order, product, dose, label, and administration identities remain aligned.
References official records without replacing them.

Invariants.Rule: AURORA-17 is a fictional radioligand-therapy candidate used only for controlled architecture and assurance demonstration.
The demonstration uses synthetic records, mock identities, simulated evidence, and no company production data.
Evidence cannot bind until the regulated object, actor, action, and source-system references are identifiable.
Critical evidence packages support hashing, later rehash verification, and explicit integrity-mismatch states.
A lifecycle stage cannot progress when mandatory dependencies remain unknown, unsatisfied, mismatched, delayed, or held.
Binding actions require present, valid, current, in-scope authority and identifiable human accountability.
No response, missed alerts, absent objection, unavailable approvers, and silent dashboards do not create authorization.
Insufficient evidence, identity, dependencies, authority, timing, or accountability creates an explicit hold, escalation, or documented pause.
Platform B or Platform B1 may evaluate admissibility but does not execute the regulated action.
Qualified humans and authorized organizational roles remain responsible for approval, release, escalation, rejection, and binding decisions.
Official execution and final records remain in governed source systems.
RAMAT Vision displays evaluated assurance state and does not approve, release, override, resolve, execute, or become evidence authority.
Platform B v1 and Thread D v1 remain architecture locked.
IRLT, DSCSA, and Compounding Pharmacy remain explicit first-tier commercialization and demonstration tracks.
